explanation: Compared against Conjecture 6.3 of Telgarsky, 'Central Binomial Tail Bounds' (arXiv:0911.2077): when p ∈ (0, 1/2) and m is even, P[B(p, m) >= m/2] >= 1 - Φ((1/2 - p)√m/σ) + ½·C(m, m/2)·σ^m, with B(p, m) a binomial count of m flips of a bias-p coin, σ = √(p(1-p)), and Φ the standard normal CDF. The statement takes m = 2k with k > 0 (m = 0 is a harmless degenerate exclusion), p ∈ (0, 1/2), σ = √(p(1-p)), Φ = cdf of gaussianReal 0 1, the left side 1 - Φ((1/2 - p)·√(2k)/σ) + (1/2)·C(2k, k)·σ^{2k}, and the right side the binomial(2k, p) measure of {k, ..., 2k}, i.e. P[B >= m/2] (non-strict, as in the paper). Faithful; the solved tag cites a Lean proof by Logical Intelligence.
